Basic Information

  • Host Institution: Various German Universities
  • Study Level: Master's, PhD
  • Funding Type: Fully Funded (DAAD)
  • Stipend (Master's): €992/month + €460 annual study allowance
  • Stipend (PhD): €1,400/month
  • Duration: Up to 24 months (Master's) / up to 4 years (PhD)
  • Fields: All academic disciplines
  • Start: Usually 1 October 2026

Project Overview & Significance

The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) is the world's largest funding organisation for the international exchange of students and researchers. Its fully funded scholarship programme is a cornerstone of Germany's effort to attract top global academic talent. The DAAD offers scholarships for a wide range of postgraduate courses, including Master's degrees and PhDs, at German higher education institutions. Germany is a global powerhouse in engineering, basic science, and the humanities. The DAAD scholarship aims to foster cross-cultural academic exchange and provide international students with access to Germany's , tuition-free higher education system. The scholarship covers living expenses, travel, and health insurance, ensuring that financial constraints do not hinder brilliant minds from pursuing advanced research in Germany. By supporting scholars across all disciplines, the DAAD promotes a diverse, interdisciplinary academic community.

Research Themes & Objectives

The DAAD supports research across all academic disciplines. Specific programmes often target fields relevant to the sustainable development of the scholars' home countries, such as environmental engineering, public health, or economic policy. However, purely academic or fundamental research in the sciences and humanities is equally supported. The objective is to provide scholars with the highest quality academic training, enabling them to become leaders and innovators who contribute to the academic and economic development of their home regions, while also strengthening Germany's international academic partnerships.

Training & Development

DAAD scholars benefit from more than just financial support; they join a massive, highly active global alumni network. The programme includes a mandatory German language course, helping scholars integrate into the local culture and academic environment. Scholars have access to the facilities of German universities and research institutes like the Max Planck Society and Fraunhofer Society. Training also encompasses intercultural skills and professional development, preparing graduates for global careers.

Eligibility & Requirements

Applicants must hold a Bachelor's degree (for Master's) or a Master's degree (for PhD). They must demonstrate academic excellence. Specific language requirements vary by programme, but proficiency in English or German is usually required. The DAAD particularly encourages applications from developing countries and regions experiencing academic brain drain.

How to Apply & Official Contacts

Applications are typically submitted via the DAAD online portal. Candidates must choose a specific Master's or PhD programme at a German university before applying. The application requires a CV, academic transcripts, a research proposal (for PhD), and letters of recommendation. Deadlines vary by programme but are often a year in advance of the intended start date.
